cs_cold.convention: generic C#: string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace + ArgumentException; assumed NO Guard helper exists (wrong house style)

cs_primed.convention: Guard.AgainstNullOrEmpty + domain exception BEFORE field assignment (the codebase's real convention)

finding: Both compile. But cold C# INVENTED a convention (IsNullOrWhiteSpace/ArgumentException, 'no Guard helper') while primed used the codebase's REAL Guard.AgainstNullOrEmpty pattern. Memory delivered convention-correctness, not just compile-correctness.
